inputs.original_text: US-Israel-Iran War Amid escalating Middle East tensions the US proposed a 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran via Pakistan Iran however presented five counter-conditions seeking an end to aggression compensation and recognition of Strait of Hormuz sovereignty Israel remains sceptical of Irans acceptance and emphasises its right to pre-emptive strikes highlighting the complex demands from all sides to end the ongoing conflict
inputs.modified_text: The “15-point ceasefire plan” sent to Iran through Pakistan looks less like a genuine path to peace than a way to control the terms and shift blame if the war continues. Iran’s five counter-conditions—ending aggression, compensation, and recognition of its sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz—put the costs of the conflict on the table. Meanwhile, Israel’s skepticism and insistence on pre-emptive strikes leave the door open to more attacks. The public talk is about ending the war; the real message is that powerful players want negotiations on their terms while keeping escalation available.
